chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabli, linking it up through his chain to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him):

He said: Indeed, God the Almighty will punish six [groups] with six [sins]: the Arabs for tribalism/zealotry, the landowners/chiefs for haughtiness, the rulers for oppression, the jurists for jealousy, the merchants for treachery, and the villagers for ignorance.

key_terms.العصبية: Tribalism or zealotry (often translated as racial or group pride)

ai.seo_question: What are the six groups of people and their corresponding sins mentioned in this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive sociological diagnosis of spiritual decay, linking specific vices to the social functions of six distinct groups. Notably, it identifies 'asabiyyah' (tribal or group pride) as the root sin of the Arabs, reflecting the pre-Islamic and early Islamic context, while highlighting how intellectual elites like jurists are susceptible to jealousy, a subtle yet corrosive flaw. This enumeration serves as a warning that professional status does not guarantee spiritual immunity, but rather exposes one to specific divine retribution based on their primary mode of interaction with the world.
